notes.decision: Preserved as 'ornament.' These ⲟⲧ glyphs appear to be decorative section-marking sigils framing the embedded chapter heading. They do not translate as ordinary lexical items.
Standard Kephalaia narrative-frame opener: 'Once again the Apostle said.' ⲡⲁⲭⲉ is Lyc. ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ 'he said' (per glossary entry ⲡⲁⲭⲉϩ 'he said').
Translated 'the first nature.' †ϣⲁⲣⲡ̄ = ⲧϣⲁⲣⲡ̄ 'the first' (fem.); ⲙⲫⲩⲥⲓⲥ = ⲛ̄ⲫⲩⲥⲓⲥ. The kephalaion identifies envy (φθόνος) as the primordial nature of the Darkness.

Translated 'she envied' (perfect 3sg.f). The unnamed feminine subject across the kephalaion is Envy/Sin/Hyle as a personified cosmic principle — confirmed by line 19 ⲡⲉⲥⲫⲑⲟⲛⲟⲥ 'her envy' and line 24 ⲡⲟⲛⲏⲣⲓⲁ 'her wickedness.' The verb (Greek loan φθονέω) recurs as the structuring formula of this entire section. 'Envy' as cosmic principle is left lowercase on the verbal form but the agent is implicitly Sin/Matter.

Parsed as relative-perfect ⲉⲧⲁⲥ- + ⲓⲁⲣⲍ + 3sg.m. obj. -ϩ̄ where ⲓⲁⲣⲍ is Lycopolitan reflex of ⲉⲓⲱⲣϩ̄ 'look at, behold, gaze upon' (cf. accumulated ⲣⲉϩⲓ̈ⲱⲣⲍ 'watcher'). Translated 'which she beheld' — Envy gazes upon the icon of the Ambassador and copies its character.

Greek χαρακτήρ + εἰκών. Translated 'character of the icon' preserving the Greek technical-rhetorical pair: the κharakter (impressed mark) of the eikōn (the Ambassador's revealed image). This is the Manichaean myth of Hyle stamping a debased copy of the upper Ambassador's beauty onto the fleshly Adam-figure.

ⲭⲡⲟ = Lyc. ϫⲡⲟ 'beget, offspring' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲭⲡⲟ ⲛ̄ⲧⲥⲩⲛⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ 'begetting of intercourse'). The reflexive 'her own very (begetting)' marks the fleshly icon as Hyle's self-generated counterfeit, in deliberate contrast to the Ambassador's emanated icon she envied.

ⲧⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'snatch, seize' (in glossary as ⲧⲱⲣⲡⲝ̄ 'the snatching') + ⲛⲧⲟⲟⲧϥ̄ 'from his hand' + ⲟⲩⲟ̄ⲁⲙ 'a power' (Lyc. = ϫⲟⲙ). The Manichaean myth of Eve's begetting: Envy snatches a light-power from Adam's hand and uses it to fashion Eve as the rib-counterpart.
ⲙⲁⲍϩⲧⲁⲩ = Lyc. ordinal 'fourth' (cf. ⲙⲁⲍⲩⲧⲟⲉ in glossary; -ϩⲧⲁⲩ from ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ 'the four'). Construction parallels ⲡⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲛⲥⲁⲡ ⲁⲛ 'the third time also' in line 6.
Lyc. ⲕⲱⲍ = Sah. ⲕⲱϩ 'be jealous, be zealous (against), envy' — semantic synonym of ⲣ̄ⲫⲑⲟⲛⲉ in this very passage. The standard ⲍ-for-ϩ Lyc. orthographic feature.

Tentatively parsed as Lyc. infinitive ⲁ-ⲡⲱϩ 'to reach, to attain (within them)' — the wickedness reaching/penetrating their thought through the purpose-of-heart of Envy. ⲡⲱϩ as a verb of penetrative reaching fits the moral-psychological context where Envy implants itself in their inner thought. Alternative parsings (ⲣⲱⲕϩ 'burn,' ⲕⲱϩ 'be jealous') are also possible.

Translated literally 'at the end of God' — likely meaning the eschatological end-time appointed by God, or the last divine envoy (Mani as the seal of the prophets). Manichaean apocalyptic register: ⲍⲁⲏ 'the end' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲥⲏⲩ ⲛ̄ⲧⲍⲁⲏ 'the time of the end'). The bitterness with which Envy responds to this final divine action motivates her envy of Mani in the next clause.

ⲕⲁⲍ here = Coptic ⲕⲁⲥ/ⲕⲱⲥ 'gall, bitterness, anger' rather than ⲕⲁϩ 'land' — supported by the affective-internal idiom 'in her bitterness within her' and parallel ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧⲥ̄ 'within her' in line 19. ⲛ̄ⲉⲥ = Lyc. for ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧⲥ̄ 'within her.'

Compound ⲣⲙ̄- ('person of') + ⲙⲏⲛⲉ ('abide, remain, every-day-ness'). Translated 'constant' — one who abides steadfastly, paralleled by ⲉϩⲥⲟⲩⲧⲁⲛⲧ 'upright' and ⲉϩⲧⲁⲭⲣⲁⲓ̈ⲧ 'firmly-established.' The cluster names the perfectly-formed elect against whom Envy directs her attack.

Lyc. ⲱⲕ ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧ = ⲏⲕ ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ 'be intent of heart' (in glossary). Construction: 'let not Sin be intent of heart against [him/them]' — i.e., let Sin's hostile attention not fix upon them. Maintains the spatial-affective semantics of the heart-fixing idiom rather than substituting a bland 'attack.'
Likely future ⲛⲁ- + ⲣ̄- + ⲭⲱⲡⲉ (= Lyc. ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'become, happen'). Standard Coptic 'shall become.' The fragment is too damaged to recover the subject and predicate fully.

Translated 'they dwell/are situated' tentatively. The form is irregular Lycopolitan; likely related to ϩⲱⲡ 'be hidden' or to a stative of ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'become, be.' The contrast inside/outside in lines 2-4 indicates the verb predicates location of envy and falsehood.

Rendered 'joints' tentatively. The lexeme is unattested in glossary or standard dictionaries. Position in the inventory (stones, bones, joints) supports a hard structural body-element. Possibly related to ⲗⲁⲕ/ⲗⲁϫ 'fragment' or to a Greek-derived term for ligaments/sinews.

Rendered 'likewise/touch' tentatively. May represent Lyc. ϩⲱⲱϥ 'also' or a verb of contact. The construction 'outside however, X in the witnessings of lies' demands either an adverbial connector or a verb of dwelling/touching parallel to ϩⲩⲱⲟⲉ in line 2.
Rendered 'with wrath.' ⲩⲛⲉⲩⲧ likely Lyc. for ⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲧ/ⲱⲛⲧ̄ 'wrath, anger.' Fits the active hostility against the teacher.

Rendered 'they place their trust.' Probable Lyc. reduction of ϣⲁⲩ-(ⲟⲩ)ⲁϩ-ⲛⲁⲍ(ⲧ)ϩ̄ 'they habitually place faith/trust' (cf. ⲡⲉϩⲛⲁⲍⲧⲉ 'his faith' in glossary). The construction ⲍⲟⲩⲟ ⲩⲁϩⲛⲁⲍϩ ⲁⲡⲁⲟⲉ 'exceedingly they place trust in falsehood' fits the apostate-vs-teacher polemic.

Rendered 'in falsehood.' ⲡⲁⲟⲉ here likely a Lyc. doublet of ⲡⲟⲁⲗ 'lie/falsehood' (line 5). Cf. accumulated vocab entry tentatively glossing 'distance/far reach,' which does not fit this immediate context.
Translated 'who are diminished in power.' ⲥⲁⲃⲕ qualitative 'become small'; ⲧⲟⲁⲙ Lyc. for ϫⲟⲙ 'power.' Refers to the apostates whose spiritual capacity has shrunk.

notes.coptic_form: ⲡⲉⲧⲥⲛⲟⲩⲭⲉ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ ⲁⲧⲣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ ⲧⲏⲣⲥ̄ ⲛⲧⲉ ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄
notes.decision: Translated 'which casts him out from the entire kind of the Living One.' ⲣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ Lyc. for 'kind, form' (in glossary); ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄ 'the Living One' (the cosmic Life-principle, possibly Mother of Life). The wickedness of Matter excludes the apostate from the family of Light.

Translated 'doubt ... contend.' ⲟⲱⲧⲧ likely = Coptic ⲱⲧⲧ̄ 'doubt, waver.' ⲁⲧⲣⲓ̈ⲉ uncertain — possibly a verb of contention/disputation paired with doubt. Both are negated conjunctives describing what the wise man avoids.

Rendered 'He who shall come forth.' The verb ⲟⲁⲗⲧ is unidentified — possibly Lyc. for ⲱⲗⲧ̄ (rest, depart) or ⲟⲩⲱⲗ (go), or a future relative of an unattested motion-verb. The construction ⲉⲓ ⲍⲓⲧⲉϩⲉⲍⲏ 'comes before him' indicates a serial-verb of arriving in the presence of the apostle/teacher. The line closes the kephalaion as a sapiential statement about the faithful one who will appear before the Lord.
